From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing intake: session jitter & payload matrix (SignalForge)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the call today. To get our Dedicated sizing team a pragmatic starting point, can you fill the attached session sample (or paste the answers below) with approximate numbers for the following? We use this to model KV cache hit-rates, batching impact, and burst tail sizing. Rough is fine — we just need shapes.

1) Traffic shape
 - Average requests / minute (last 30 days):
 - Peak requests / minute (observed peak):
 - % of traffic coming from API vs UI/webhooks: (e.g., 85% API)
 - Typical dayparting (local TZ hours that carry >60% of daily load):

2) Session / concurrency
 - Average active sessions (concurrent open sessions):
 - Peak concurrent sessions:
 - Typical session duration distribution (median, p90, p99 in seconds):
 - % of sessions that are long-lived ( > 10 minutes ):

3) Prompt & response lengths
 - Median prompt tokens / request and p95/p99 tokens:
 - Median completion tokens / response and p95/p99:
 - Do you send multi-turn histories in full each request or rely on session-based KV cache?

4) Latency & SLOs
 - Desired p95 generation latency (ms)
 - Acceptable p99 hit to fallback (ms) or fallback model guidance

5) KV cache / reuse
 - Estimated cache reuse rate for repeated prefixes (percent)
 - Typical KV cache TTL (seconds) if any

6) Workload special cases
 - Anything that causes large spikes (batch scoring jobs, marketing blasts, scheduled reports)?
 - Are there daily/weekly planned spikes (cron jobs)?

7) Timeline & constraints
 - Pilot target date / pilot duration
 - Procurement timeline for PO/contract
 - Any restricted models (on-prem req / data locality / encryption needs)

If you prefer, upload a CSV exported from your API logs with columns: timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, session_id, model_family, latency_ms. I attached a simple template SF_session_sample.csv.

Once we have these, our sizing runbook will return a recommended reserved pool (GPU count & SKU guidance), expected throughput under your SLO, and a suggested canary plan.

Thanks — I’ve cc'd Marissa (solutions eng) to pick up the technical workshop scheduling once we have the sample.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: olivia@signalforge.ai

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake: session jitter & payload matrix (SignalForge)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks — attaching the filled sample (SF_session_sample.csv) and a short notes section inline below. High level: most traffic is API-driven, weekend traffic ~15% of weekday; we do two marketing blasts/month that spike for ~45 minutes. Pilot target is Nov 15. Procurement looped in for timeline.

Inline answers (estimates):
1) Traffic shape
 - Avg requests / min (30d): 4,800 RPM (80 r/s)
 - Peak requests / min: 28,800 RPM (480 r/s) observed during product launch
 - API vs UI: 92% API / 8% UI
 - Dayparting: 09:00–18:00 PT ~65% of daily load

2) Session / concurrency
 - Avg active sessions: 1,100
 - Peak concurrent sessions: 6,500
 - Session duration: median 35s, p90 4m, p99 18m
 - Long-lived sessions (>10m): ~6%

3) Prompt & response lengths
 - Median prompt tokens: 180; p95 640; p99 1,200
 - Median completion tokens: 40; p95 220; p99 600
 - We currently send full multi-turn history in every request for simplicity (we can change this if KV caching is available).

4) Latency & SLOs
 - Target p95 gen latency: 250ms
 - Target p99: 800ms (we expect some grace at pilot)
 - Fallback: okay to route to a slightly smaller model if latency > 2s

5) KV cache / reuse
 - Cache reuse estimate: 28% reuse on repeated prefixes (chat greetings, templated prompts)
 - No strict TTL today; sessions end with inactivity timeout ~15m

6) Workload special cases
 - Marketing blasts: ~10x baseline for 30–60 minutes, 2x baseline sustained for 6 hours after
 - Batch scoring: nightly batch of ~200k short prompts (non-real-time) — can be scheduled on lower-priority capacity

7) Timeline & constraints
 - Pilot start: target 2026-11-15 for 2-week pilot
 - Procurement expects to issue PO by 2026-11-05
 - Data residency: US only; encryption at rest required

Let us know if you want the CSV (we can export a 7-day sample). Quick Q: do you support hardware-quantized model tiers? That will matter for cost estimates.

Cheers,
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, SignalForge
olivia@signalforge.ai
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: olivia@signalforge.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake: session jitter & payload matrix (SignalForge)

Hi Olivia — super helpful, thanks. Looping Marissa (solutions) and Laura (sales lead) to align sizing and procurement milestones. A few clarifying items so we can produce a concrete reserved capacity proposal: 

1) Token throughput estimate
 - Using your med/p95 numbers and the session shapes, we’ll model an initial baseline and a stress-window for marketing blasts. Can you confirm whether the p95 completion tokens (220) are dominated by a single completion or by multi-shot responses concatenated?

2) KV caching path
 - You said you send full history today. For the pilot, would you be open to trying KV-cache for the most active session types? If yes, we can model a 'KV-enabled' scenario (saves ~18–30% tokens/sec depending on reuse).

3) Peak / sustained split
 - For burst modeling we treat marketing blasts as a 30–60m window with an initial 10x spike (as you noted). For procurement we’ll propose a reserve that covers typical peak+burst fallback routing. Is a cold-start tolerance of 10–15s for scaling acceptable for non-critical endpoints?

4) Latency SLOs and fallback
 - For p95 250ms target, our back-of-envelope suggests a reserved pool sized for steady 85% of observed peak, plus a small burstable buffer. If you can accept routing >2s to fallback for <0.5% of requests, that materially reduces committed GPUs.

Preliminary recommendation (ballpark, subject to final run):
 - Pilot reserved pool: capacity to sustain ~350 r/s at p95 (covers steady load + buffer) with a burst pool for short 10x spikes routed to lower-priority nodes.
 - Suggested pilot model family: open-llm-3 or equivalent 70B quantized tier (if that maps to your architectures) — Marissa can propose specific SKUs after a quick workshop.

Next steps: Marissa — can you schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop early next week? Laura — I’ll add a short note on PO timing once procurement confirms. Olivia — if you can export a 7-day CSV sample, that will let us run the simulator overnight and return a concrete GPU-count + burst plan by Friday.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — that all looks good. I attached a 7-day export (SF_session_sample.csv) and a draft pilot SLA (SLA-draft-SF.docx) for your review. Quick confirmations: 
- We can try a KV-caching experiment for the most active endpoints during pilot.
- Cold-start tolerance for non-critical endpoints: up to 12s acceptable.
- Procurement expects to issue PO by 2026-11-04 if pricing matches the pilot budget.

Please proceed with the overnight simulation and proposed pool sizes. We'll be available for a workshop Monday (2026-10-25) morning PT — Marissa, can you take this?

Thanks — look forward to the sizing plan.

Cheers,
Olivia
